Recognize the Problem

When every minute
matters.

Not every plumbing issue requires the same response. Explore these common emergencies and learn when to call a professional.

01
WATER DAMAGE

Burst Pipes

A burst pipe can release large amounts of water quickly. Shut off the water supply if safe and arrange professional assistance.

Call for help
02
URGENT

Flooding & Backups

Water backing up into your property needs urgent assessment to identify the source and reduce further damage.

Call for help
03
LEAK DETECTION

Major Water Leaks

Leaking pipes, valves, or plumbing connections can damage walls, ceilings, floors, and personal belongings.

Call for help
04
PROFESSIONAL HELP

Sewer Line Problems

Sewage odors, wastewater backups, or multiple blocked drains can signal a serious plumbing issue.

Call for help
Safety First

Before help
arrives.

Take these precautions only when it is safe. Never put yourself at risk to save property or reach a shutoff valve.

01

Shut off the water

Turn off the main supply if the valve is safely accessible.

02

Avoid electrical hazards

Keep away from standing water near outlets, wiring, and appliances.

03

Protect the affected area

Keep children and pets away. Move belongings only if the area is safe.

04

Explain what happened

Tell the provider where the problem is and whether water is still flowing.

Important Warning

If flooding creates an electrical hazard, move to safety and contact the appropriate emergency service. If you suspect a gas leak, leave the area immediately.

Protect People First

Property can wait.
Your safety cannot.

If safe, turn off your main water supply. Keep away from standing water near electrical equipment, protect belongings only if safe, and call a qualified plumbing professional.

Do not enter standing water or touch wet electrical equipment. Keep others away. Contact emergency services or a qualified electrician as appropriate.

Some providers charge additional fees for after-hours, weekend, or holiday calls. Ask about call-out fees, labor rates, and the estimated total before approving.

Availability varies by provider and service area. Call to confirm current operating hours, response time, and whether a technician can attend your location.
